text:
maya: kicking off LHR edge bring-up checklist. main items: TGW attachment, peering to transit, NAT gateway pool, private DNS delegation for redwood-lhr zone, and GPU fleet subnet allocations. can folks run quick validation?

kai: on it. started by checking TGW attachments and route propagation. TGW shows attachment: tgw-06abc (state: available). route table has propagated routes for 10.10.0.0/16 -> attachment.

andre: NATs: provisioning 3 NAT gateways in LHR to match AZ spread. will allocate 3 EIPs then attach to nat-01/02/03. note: EIP quota is low for this account, i requested raise — ETA 6h.

maya: thanks. EIP quota might block full egress capacity. if quota delays, we can temporarily use shared egress through core transit (higher egress cost). i'll flag cost impact once we know.

kai: quick DNS check for private zone delegation: ran 
`dig @10.0.0.2 redwood-lhr.internal. SOA +short`
response: `ns1.core.internal.` looks good, SOA ttl 900. need to confirm zone records for private service discovery (model-registry.lhr).

andre: adding records now. pushing terraform change:
```hcl
resource "aws_route53_record" "model-registry" {
  zone_id = "ZLHR123"
  name = "model-registry.lhr.internal"
  type = "A"
  ttl  = 60
  records = ["10.10.5.12"]
}
```
apply in progress.

ops-bot: infra-checker finished: TGW routes OK; Transit peering latency baseline 12ms; NAT gateways pending (3/3) due to EIP quota; DNS delegation detected but record propagation at 40%.

sre-jen: smoke test plan posted in runbook channel. quick smoke commands for canary GPU job:
```
kubectl run --rm -it --image=redwood/gpu-test:latest gpu-smoke -- nvidia-smi -L && curl -sS http://model-registry.lhr.internal/health
```
ran canary on subset of nodes (3 g4dn-like instances) -> nvidia-smi ok, model-registry returned 200, but observed 502 from endpoint via shared egress path. suspect route preference fallback to core transit.

maya: that 502 matches the temporary egress path. once NATs are up and correct SNAT rules applied, traffic should source from local EIPs and bypass transit. andre, any ETA on EIP raise?

andre: raise approved, AWS allocated 3 EIPs. attaching now. terraform apply finished: nat-01/02/03 in-service.

ops-bot: infra-checker re-run: NAT gateways attached (3/3), route tables updated, SNAT mappings present.

kai: re-run smoke: kubectl canary -> model-registry 200, external fetches succeed, traceroute to external model repo shows egress via nat-01 (EIP 54.72.xx.xx).

sre-jen: perf baseline for LHR GPU fleet: cold start 280ms p95, steady state token latency 42ms p95 for short prompts. noted in runbook.

maya: nice. two outstanding items: 1) confirm BGP prop to peering partner for cross-region fallback (pinged partner, waiting on their side), 2) cost note: LHR egress pricing higher than IAD; recommend applying per-route egress routing policy for heavy-throughput models to prefer IAD if latency budget allows.

andre: filed routing policy PR to prefer lower-cost region for batch workloads. will add canary allowlist for latency sensitive routes.

maya: handing off to oncall for monitoring: set alert for NAT EIP exhaustion, TGW attachment flaps, and model-registry 5xx rate >1% for 5m. tagging @oncall for first 72h. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: alerting playbook linked: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/lhr-bringup. handoff recorded in incident history.

maya: thanks team — I'll close the ticket after 24h stable metrics. :white_check_mark:
